knowledge:
- key_parameters: dataDir=Path to the parent directory containing class-specific subdirectories of raw LC/MS files ;; project=Character string defining the project name, which determines the output results folder name ;; adductTable=Set to "negAdducts" for negative ionization mode annotation, or left NULL/default for positive mode ;; pvalue=P-value threshold for selecting statistically significant features ;; peakPrecision=Mass tolerance window (in mass/charge units) used during the biotransformations annotation step ;; peakTolerance=Mass tolerance window (in mass/charge units) used for matching features against the metabolite database ;; spectraEstimation=Logical flag in MAITbuilder indicating whether to group imported peaks into pseudospectra
- alternatives: XCMS=Used internally by MAIT for peak detection, grouping, and retention time correction ;; CAMERA=Used for initial peak correlation and adduct annotation, which MAIT extends with biotransformations ;; MetaboAnalyst/XCMS Online=Web-based alternatives that are less programmable and require manual step-by-step intervention
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have raw LC/MS data files (or pre-processed peak tables) and want to identify statistically significant metabolites that differentiate sample classes, validate their predictive power using machine learning classifiers (SVM, PLS-DA, KNN), and generate automated profiling plots.
- pitfalls: Directory structure=Raw files must be organized into subdirectories named after their respective sample classes under a single parent directory ;; Polarity mismatch=Failing to set adductTable="negAdducts" or polarity="negative" when analyzing negative ionization mode data will result in incorrect positive-mode annotations ;; Step dependency=Biotransformations and metabolite identification functions require a MAIT object that has already undergone peak annotation and statistical feature selection.

workflows.name: raw_lcms_end_to_end_pipeline
workflows.intent: Perform end-to-end analysis of raw LC/MS data files from peak detection to metabolite identification and validation.
input: raw_data_dir/ (parent directory containing subdirectories of raw LC/MS files like CDF, organized by class)
workflows.stages: 1. Peak detection and retention time correction ;; 2. Peak annotation and pseudospectra grouping ;; 3. Statistical feature selection ;; 4. Visualization and plotting ;; 5. Biotransformation annotation ;; 6. Database-driven metabolite identification ;; 7. Cross-validation of significant features
workflows.code:
library(MAIT)
library(faahKO)
cdfFiles<-system.file("cdf", package="faahKO", mustWork=TRUE)
MAIT <- sampleProcessing(dataDir = cdfFiles, project = "MAIT_Demo", 
snThres=2,rtStep=0.03)
MAIT <- peakAnnotation(MAIT.object = MAIT,corrWithSamp = 0.7, 
corrBetSamp = 0.75,perfwhm = 0.6)
MAIT<- spectralSigFeatures(MAIT.object = MAIT,pvalue=0.05,
       p.adj="none",scale=FALSE)
signTable <- sigPeaksTable(MAIT.object = MAIT, printCSVfile = FALSE)
plotBoxplot(MAIT)
plotHeatmap(MAIT)
MAIT<-plotPCA(MAIT,plot3d=FALSE)
MAIT<-plotPLS(MAIT,plot3d=FALSE)
PLSmodel <- model(MAIT, type = "PLS")
PCAmodel <- model(MAIT, type = "PCA")
Biotransformations(MAIT.object = MAIT, peakPrecision = 0.005) 
MAIT <- identifyMetabolites(MAIT.object = MAIT, peakTolerance = 0.005)
metTable<-metaboliteTable(MAIT)
MAIT <- Validation(Iterations = 20, trainSamples= 3, 
MAIT.object = MAIT)
classifRatioClasses(MAIT)

workflows.name: external_peak_table_analysis
workflows.intent: Import pre-processed external peak tables, masses, and retention times to perform annotation and metabolite identification.
input: peaks_matrix (numeric matrix of peak intensities across samples)
masses_vector (numeric vector of peak m/z values)
rt_vector (numeric vector of peak retention times in minutes)
workflows.stages: 1. Build MAIT object from external data ;; 2. Perform biotransformation and adduct annotation ;; 3. Identify metabolites against the database
workflows.code:
peaks <- scores(MAIT)
masses <- getPeaklist(MAIT)$mz
rt <- getPeaklist(MAIT)$rt/60
importMAIT <- MAITbuilder(data = peaks, masses = masses, 
              rt = rt,significantFeatures = TRUE, 
              spectraEstimation = TRUE,rtRange=0.2,
              corThresh=0.7)
importMAIT <- Biotransformations(MAIT.object = importMAIT, 
              adductAnnotation = TRUE, 
              peakPrecision = 0.005, adductTable = NULL)
importMAIT <- identifyMetabolites(MAIT.object = importMAIT, 
              peakTolerance=0.005,polarity="positive")
